id_and_class.theory_title: Locke’s Reflexive Consciousness and the Making of the Person
id_and_class.summary: John Locke defines consciousness as ‘the perception of what passes in a man’s own mind’, an immediate self-awareness built into every perception rather than a separate faculty or second act. He locates personal identity in sameness of consciousness, not in sameness of body or soul, which makes the person a unit of moral accountability. He stays agnostic about whether the thing that thinks is matter or an immaterial soul.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Self-Aware Perception That Makes the Person

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a self-intimating feature internal to every perception of an idea: to perceive is to perceive that one perceives. It is neither a substance, nor a faculty, nor a separate higher-order thought.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Locke holds that we cannot tell whether God has joined an immaterial thinking substance to the body or given suitably organized matter the power to think. He judged an immaterial soul more probable, but his account of consciousness and personal identity does not depend on it.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Undetermined (thinking may be superadded to organized matter or annexed to an immaterial soul, and Locke holds we cannot know which)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Every sensation or thought includes tacit awareness of oneself as its subject, which gives each person intuitive certainty of their own present existence. Ideas are the immediate objects of perception.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Simple ideas such as color, warmth, and pain are received passively and cannot be made or broken down by the mind. Secondary qualities (colors, sounds, tastes) exist as ideas produced by powers in bodies and need not resemble their physical causes, though Locke does not explain why corpuscular motion should produce any feeling at all.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Ideas of sensation and reflection, an unknown substance that supports thinking (material or immaterial), bodies with primary qualities and powers, and persons as distinct from both organisms and souls.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: All ideas come from experience, through sensation of external objects or reflection on the mind’s own operations. Consciousness of one’s own thinking is immediate and noninferential.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Simple ideas, received passively, which the mind compares, combines, abstracts, and relates into complex ideas. Persons are built by consciousness extending backward to appropriate past experiences and actions as one’s own.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (simple ideas); self-awareness; personal identity over time; moral agency and accountability.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Reflexive awareness intrinsic to thinking, combined with ‘appropriation’: present consciousness extends to past experiences and owns them, chiefly through memory, and this sameness of consciousness constitutes the person.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Thinking is an operation of the soul, not its essence, so consciousness can lapse, as in dreamless sleep. Locke rejects the Cartesian claim that the soul always thinks with the quip that ‘every drowsy nod shakes their doctrine’.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness ties actions to a self concerned with its own future happiness and misery, which grounds accountability, reward, punishment, and repentance. Locke calls this practical concern ‘concernment’.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Locke explains how consciousness unifies a person across time but does not explain the unity of simultaneous experiences.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Experience enters as simple ideas through sensation and reflection. The mind then builds complex ideas, and qualitative appearance is separated from the microphysical structure of the bodies that cause it.
core_claims_and_evidence: Thinking consists in being conscious that one thinks, so a wholly unnoticed thought is scarcely intelligible as thought.
Personal identity consists in sameness of consciousness, not sameness of body or immaterial substance.
In the prince-and-cobbler case, if the prince’s consciousness entered the cobbler’s body, the person would be the prince while the man would be the cobbler.
Colors, sounds, and tastes are ideas produced by powers in bodies, whereas solidity, extension, figure, motion, and number resemble features of bodies.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and introspective, framed by empiricist epistemology and thought experiments.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Butler charged that defining identity by remembered consciousness is circular, and Reid’s ‘brave officer’ case suggests such identity is not transitive across memory gaps. Evidence for unconscious perception, cognition, and motivation undermines Locke’s equation of thinking with consciousness.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Locke does not explain the unity of simultaneous experience, how qualitative character is produced, or what kind of thing a consciousness that can persist through changes of substance is. Interpreters dispute whether sameness of consciousness reduces to memory.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: The view individuates persons by consciousness before settling what bears it, which keeps it consistent with either materialism or dualism. Its placement under Materialism reflects its influence on later thinkers; Locke himself thought an immaterial soul more probable.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Locke allows that God could give suitably organized matter the power to think, but he holds that we cannot know whether thinking belongs to matter or to an immaterial soul.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Locke thought an immaterial soul more probable, and on his view a person survives wherever the same consciousness continues, whatever substance carries it.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Since the person follows sameness of consciousness rather than substance, a new substrate would preserve the person only if the same consciousness, owning its past, continued in it.
